Definition: Integration of CRVS data (births, deaths, marriages) into data exchange for real-time verification and service eligibility
Comments: Civil Registry Code dates from 1967 and has not been modernized. No digital CRVS system documented. World Bank diagnostic notes outdated legal framework with updates pending since 2006. The ENTD.GW strategy plans to address this as part of digital public services pillar but no operational system.
revision_notes: Original score (1, Not integrated, 2022) rested on a World Bank 2022 diagnostic predating recent activity. A June 2025 interview with the Head of the Civil Registration Office (Biometric Update) confirms the SIREC digital civil registration system was launched in January 2025 (covering births, deaths, marriages and unions), replacing paper registers, and that officials are actively exploring integration of the digitised birth registration system with the health and education sectors. No operational cross-government data exchange drawing on CRVS data is yet documented, but active planning for integration is confirmed by a primary interview source, warranting an upgrade from 'Not integrated' to 'Planned'. The 2025-2030 ENTD.GW national digital strategy (Decree 10/2025) also references future service integration.
revised_comments: Guinea-Bissau launched its Integrated System of Citizen Registers and Statistics (SIREC) in January 2025, digitising civil registration records for births, marriages and deaths and replacing paper-based registers, starting at the first Bissau conservatória. Officials at the Ministry of Justice's Civil Registration Office confirm they are actively exploring integration of the digitised birth registration system with the health and education sectors, though no operational cross-government data exchange currently draws on CRVS data. Integration into a wider data exchange remains at the planning stage.

Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: No digital ID scheme exists. The Civil Registry Code dates from 1967 (pre-independence), with updates pending since 2006. World Bank Digital Economy Diagnostic 2022 states 'Absence of a structured foundational identity system prevents digital ID development.' No integration possible without foundational system.
revision_notes: The original comment stated 'no digital ID scheme exists', which understates the position: Guinea-Bissau in fact has a longstanding national biometric identity card system operated in partnership with Semlex, with 18 biometric enrolment/production centres nationwide as of early 2026. However, no evidence was found that this ID system is technically integrated with any cross-government data exchange platform for identity verification or authentication - a June 2025 interview describes an 'integrated digital identity system' as a goal for 'the next few years', not a current capability. The score of 1 (Not integrated) is therefore confirmed on the data-exchange-integration criterion specifically, but the comments are revised to correct the factual record on ID system existence.
revised_comments: Guinea-Bissau operates a national biometric identity card system, run in partnership with Semlex, with biometric enrolment and card-production centres in Bissau and across the regions (18 centres nationwide by early 2026). This foundational ID system is not currently integrated with any cross-government data exchange for identity verification or authentication; officials describe an integrated digital identity system as a medium-term goal rather than a current capability, contingent on further digitisation of civil registration (the SIREC system, launched January 2025) and the wider ENTD.GW 2025-2030 digital transformation strategy.

Definition: Integration of health records, patient registration, immunization data, and health insurance into data exchange
Comments: No operational digital health platform documented. World Bank diagnostic found low digital competency in public sector generally. Health sector is not mentioned as having digital exchange capabilities. The ENTD.GW strategy includes health in its digital public services pillar but this is prospective.
revision_notes: Original score of 1 (Not integrated, 2022) is now outdated. Zenysis Technologies confirmed (May 2024 press release, corroborated by an INASA president quote) a partnership building the National Integration and Analytics (NIA) Platform to integrate over 20 previously fragmented health data systems used by INASA and MINSAP into a single workspace. Separately, Antares Vision Group signed a multi-year agreement (February 2025) with the Ministry of Health to build a National Medicines Verification & Authentication System, including a Customs & Import Bridge linking customs records to manufacturer transactions and a Central Registry, rolling out under a National Digital Health Strategy launched in January 2025, with mandatory registration effective March 2026. These are genuine, actively-implemented technical integration efforts rather than mere planning, justifying an upgrade to 'Under development' (3). No evidence yet of full operational integration into a cross-government exchange, so 'Partially integrated' (4) is not yet warranted.
revised_comments: Guinea-Bissau's health sector is undergoing active data integration under a National Digital Health Strategy launched in January 2025. The National Integration and Analytics (NIA) Platform, built with Zenysis Technologies for INASA and the Ministry of Public Health, is consolidating more than 20 previously fragmented health data systems into a single workspace to support real-time disease monitoring. In parallel, a pharmaceutical traceability system built with Antares Vision Group links a National Medicines Catalogue, a Customs & Import Bridge and a Central Registry of supply-chain actors, with mandatory registration due to take effect in March 2026. DHIS2 has been used for malaria and routine health data since 2014-2015 across more than 145 facilities. These initiatives represent health data integration actively under development rather than a fully operational cross-government data exchange.

Definition: Integration with national payment systems for government-to-person (G2P), government-to-business (G2B) transactions via data exchange
Comments: Mobile money usage increased 77% in 2020 but no national digital financial services priority exists. Kontaktu (tax filing/payment system) is operational (homegrown). SIGFIP financial management partially adopted. No e-payments or e-transactions law. No interoperability with regional payment systems. The World Bank WARDIP project and ENTD.GW plan to address digital payments as a priority.
revision_notes: Score of 2 (Planned) confirmed. BCEAO's regional Interoperable Instant Payment System Platform (PI-SPI) launched officially on 30 September 2025, connecting banks (Coris Bank, Ecobank, Orabank), microfinance institutions and e-money issuers across UEMOA, including participating Guinea-Bissau institutions - this improves the underlying payments interoperability landscape but is a BCEAO regional retail-payments initiative, not evidence of a national data exchange integrating G2P/G2B government payments. ENTD.GW 2025-2030 (Decree 10/2025) reiterates digital payments as a strategic objective, but implementation for government payment integration specifically remains at the planning/strategy stage. No evidence found of an operational or under-development G2P/G2B data exchange integration, so the code stays at 'Planned'.
revised_comments: Digital payments integration into a national data exchange remains at the planning stage. Guinea-Bissau's homegrown Kontaktu tax platform and partially adopted SIGFIP financial management system provide some digitised public financial functions, and Guinea-Bissau banks now participate in BCEAO's regional Interoperable Instant Payment System Platform (PI-SPI), launched in September 2025, which connects banks, microfinance institutions and mobile money issuers across UEMOA. However, integration of national payment systems for government-to-person or government-to-business transactions via a dedicated data exchange has not moved beyond planning, with the 2025-2030 ENTD.GW national digital transformation strategy identifying digital payments as a future priority.

Definition: Extent to which the data exchange enables services accessible to all population groups including persons with disabilities, elderly, low literacy
Comments: Digital services are extremely limited. Internet penetration 32.5% (2023). Most services are manual/offline. Universal Service Fund (USF) exists but is underutilized, lacking transparency and targeting. No digital ID, no e-services accessible to most citizens. Digital literacy is very low.
revision_notes: Score of 1 (Limited accessibility) confirmed. DataReportal's Digital 2026 report puts internet penetration at 32.5% as of late 2025 (734,000 users), essentially unchanged from the 32.5% figure cited for 2023 - i.e. the original data point remains current and accurate rather than stale. No evidence of dedicated accessibility measures for persons with disabilities, the elderly or low-literacy users; digital services remain overwhelmingly manual/offline. Confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Digital services in Guinea-Bissau remain accessible to only a small share of the population. Internet penetration stood at 32.5% at the end of 2025 (DataReportal), with the large majority of citizens relying on manual, in-person government services. No dedicated accessibility provisions for persons with disabilities, the elderly or low-literacy users have been identified in relation to the data exchange or associated e-services, and the Universal Service Fund intended to extend access remains underutilised and lacking in transparency.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: Draft laws for data privacy and cybercrime exist but not promulgated as of World Bank diagnostic 2022. No government data center or disaster recovery center exists; data stored on individual ministry servers without shared infrastructure. ENTD.GW plans data centers and e-gov by 2030. No enforced data sovereignty provisions in place.
revision_notes: Score of 1 (No controls) confirmed. A February 2025 report (RTP Africa) shows the government still seeking to adopt specific personal-data-protection legislation, meaning no enacted data protection or localisation law existed as of that date. A 2025 cybersecurity feasibility study (Cybil Portal) confirms Guinea-Bissau is still at the assessment/tender-preparation stage for a national CERT, Critical Information Infrastructure protection and a National GovCloud - none of which are yet operational. No enforceable data sovereignty/localisation provisions found. Confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Guinea-Bissau has no enforced data sovereignty or localisation provisions in place. As of early 2025 the government was still seeking to adopt legislation to protect citizens' personal data on digital platforms, and a 2025 feasibility study found the country at the assessment and tender-preparation stage for foundational cybersecurity infrastructure, including a national CERT, critical information infrastructure protection and a National GovCloud, none of which are yet operational. Government data continues to be held on individual ministry servers without shared, secured infrastructure, and the ENTD.GW 2025-2030 strategy envisages data centres and stronger governance only as future objectives.
